capture.final_message:
Use the universal Laurent-polynomial representation of Chebyshev polynomials. Under the substitution \(X=z+z^{-1}\),

\[
T_k(X)\longmapsto z^k+z^{-k}\qquad(k\in\mathbb Z).
\]

Then composition becomes multiplication of indices:

\[
T_m(T_n(z+z^{-1}))
 =T_m(z^n+z^{-n})
 =z^{mn}+z^{-mn}
 =T_{mn}(z+z^{-1}).
\]

Injectivity of \(R[X]\to R[z,z^{-1}]\), \(X\mapsto z+z^{-1}\), recovers the polynomial identity. Equivalently, prove it universally over \(\mathbb Z\) and transport it to every commutative ring by coefficient mapping.

For the first conjunct, simply unfold the recurrence for the second-kind normalization:

\[
S_0=1,\qquad S_1=X,\qquad S_{k+1}=X S_k-S_{k-1},
\]

which immediately gives \(S_2=X^2-1\).

Thus the useful intermediate goals are the Laurent evaluation formula for \(T_k\), its compatibility with replacing \(z\) by \(z^n\), and injectivity/naturality of the substitution. This algebraic route is essential because the theorem holds over arbitrary commutative rings, where trigonometric arguments and division are unavailable.
